metadata.deduplication_note: Three lenses independently reported DestinationPolicy.cs:118 (COR-002, SEC-002, TST-002) and three reported ValidateDestination.cs:95 (COR-005, SEC-004, TST-003). Merged, most severe kept, all reporting agents recorded. DnsHostResolver.cs:60 was reported by COR-001 (critical) and TST-006 (warning) for distinct defects at the same line; merged under the critical with the second defect preserved in the description.
metadata.agent_self_reported_limitation: review-testing had no shell tool and could not run git diff, so its rule 2 assessment (deleted or weakened tests) was made from the working tree and the handover's planned-vs-actual table rather than from the commit history. It said so rather than implying full coverage.

findings.title: STD-SEC-05 — the redirect path validates scheme only, and no waiver existed
findings.description: STD-SEC-05 requires validation against permitted schemes and hosts immediately before issuing a redirect. CheckScheme performs no host check. The brainstorm justified this with 'we never fetch the destination server-side', which answers the SSRF half of the rule's rationale but not the phishing half. standards/waivers.md read '_None._', and the plan's Known Constraint is not a waiver.
findings.suggestion: Re-validate fully on the redirect path with a cached verdict, or record a waiver with approver and expiry.
findings.reason: Waiver written rather than code changed. WVR-001 in standards/waivers.md, scoped to the redirect path only, approver ReposVijay, expiry 2026-11-17, follow-up #19. The agent's core point is accepted: the plan's accepted-residual-risk note was not a waiver and this rule was being deviated from without a record. The creation path is not waived.

findings.title: IPv6 reserved ranges and IPv4-embedding encodings are permitted
findings.description: IsPermittedV6 refuses only ::1, ::, fe80::/10, fec0::/10 and fc00::/7. Permitted today: ff00::/8 multicast including SSDP-over-v6, ::a.b.c.d IPv4-compatible, 64:ff9b::/96 NAT64, 2002::/16 6to4, 2001:db8::/32. Each of the last four is a loopback or private address written in a different notation — the bypass class the ::ffff: guard exists to close, left half-implemented. AC-3's 'reserved' clause is unmet on the v6 side, as it is on the v4 side the handover probed.
findings.suggestion: Refuse by prefix rather than by named example, and judge any embedded IPv4 value on what it embeds. Add theory rows for ff02::1, ff05::c, ::10.0.0.1, 64:ff9b::a00:1, 2002:0a00:0001:: and 2001:db8::1, keeping a public v6 address permitted.
findings.reason: Three independent lenses reached the same line. Fixing.

findings.title: HostResolution.NotFound is unreachable on the real resolver path
findings.description: Dns.GetHostAddressesAsync throws SocketException with SocketErrorCode HostNotFound for a nonexistent host rather than returning an empty array. The blanket catch maps it to Failed, so NotFound is dead code in production and every mistyped hostname is reported as a transient failure telling the caller to retry something that will never work. It also inflates the counter meant to signal our own resolver is in trouble. The branch's own test pins the defect: it throws SocketException(11001), which is HostNotFound, and asserts Failed. TST-006 additionally reports at this line that the ArgumentException arm is untested and that unlisted exception types escape unchanged, breaching layers.md 6.3.
findings.suggestion: Split the catch on SocketErrorCode: HostNotFound and NoData map to NotFound; the rest to Failed. Change the existing test to throw a genuinely transient code and add one asserting HostNotFound maps to NotFound.
findings.reason: A test that locks in a defect is worse than no test. Fixing both the mapping and the test that pinned it.

findings.title: Unsynchronised counter state can hang a request thread
findings.description: Total++ is a non-atomic read-modify-write and _byKind[refusal] = For(refusal) + 1 is check-then-act on a plain Dictionary, on an instance whose only sensible lifetime is singleton. Lost updates under load are certain; worse, concurrent resize can corrupt the bucket chain and spin a request thread indefinitely inside FindEntry. That is a hang on the creation path caused by a telemetry side effect, which STD-OPS-04 exists to prevent.
findings.suggestion: ConcurrentDictionary with AddOrUpdate, Interlocked.Increment for the total, and a Parallel.For test asserting the tally.
findings.reason: STD-OPS-04 is critical severity and this is a hang, not merely a miscount. Fixing.

findings.title: STD-SEC-02 — no length or range validation at the trust boundary
findings.description: The rule requires every externally-originated value to be validated for type, range, length and format at the point it enters the system. Only type and format are checked, and those inside Domain code rather than before it. An unbounded string reaches DNS resolution and the log.
findings.suggestion: Add an explicit length cap as the first guard, before parsing, resolution or logging, with a test asserting an over-length destination is refused without the resolver being called.
findings.reason: Cheap to fix and the rule is explicit about all four checks. Fixing.

findings.title: AC-5 is unproven on the scheme and parse rejection path
findings.description: Every telemetry test drives an address or resolution refusal, so the early-return branch carrying SchemeNotPermitted and NotAbsoluteUrl emits telemetry nothing asserts. Removing Record from that branch keeps all 93 tests green, while silently removing telemetry from the rejection class that matters most operationally — javascript: and data: destinations are the probing traffic the counter exists to surface.
findings.suggestion: Add telemetry cases driving a scheme refusal and a parse refusal through the fully-constructed handler.
findings.reason: An acceptance criterion that a green suite does not protect is not proven. Fixing.

findings.title: Log is not structured, carries the raw URL including credentials, and no trace identifier
findings.description: Merged from three lenses. The generic Log overload is called with a bare string as TState, so {Reason}, {Host} and {Addresses} never bind to any property and AC-5's 'structured' is unmet; the template says Host while the formatter emits Url. Separately, the formatter interpolates the entire submitted URL, and SchemeTests accepts https://user:pw@example.com/path as valid, so userinfo credentials and query tokens can be written verbatim — STD-SEC-04. No traceId is passed at all, despite the class comment claiming correlation by it.
findings.suggestion: Use the structured overload with bound arguments, log the host rather than the raw URL, pass the trace identifier, and assert the bound properties in the test rather than the rendered string.
findings.reason: Deferred to a follow-up issue with the other high findings, on the user's instruction to fix criticals now and defer the rest. Recorded as the highest-value deferred item: it is three separate defects at one line, one of which (credentials in logs) is a security-pack breach, and the class comment currently asserts a correlation that does not exist. Should be first in the follow-up.

findings.title: Uri.Host hands the resolver a bracketed IPv6 literal and a Unicode IDN label
findings.description: Uri.Host preserves brackets for an IPv6 literal, so https://[2606:4700::1111]/ produces a DNS lookup for the literal string '[2606:4700::1111]', which fails and becomes Failed via the blanket catch. A legitimate public IPv6 destination is refused forever with 'try again shortly'. IdnHost is the correct property; it also handles internationalised domains.
findings.suggestion: Use IdnHost, and add an orchestration test asserting the resolver receives the unbracketed address.
findings.reason: Fails closed rather than open, so it is a wrong result on a legitimate input rather than a bypass. Deferred with the other highs.

findings.title: STD-SEC-06 — the DNS rebinding threat has no negative test
findings.description: The threat is named in both the brainstorm and the plan, and no test asserts the attack fails. The design makes such a test impossible while the redirect path checks scheme only.
findings.suggestion: Add the test once the redirect-path re-check exists, or waive.
findings.reason: Structurally dependent on SEC-001. WVR-001 accepts the underlying exposure and expires 2026-11-17; this finding expires with it, and the follow-up is tracked on #19. Deferring separately would duplicate that record.

findings.title: The information-disclosure test cannot fail, and excludes the field where a leak would occur
findings.description: From has no parameter through which an address could arrive, so asserting its literals contain no private ranges asserts a property of the test's own inputs. The scanned body also omits Errors, the caller-supplied FieldError.Reason collection, which is the most plausible place a host or address reaches a response body. The handover offers this test as the mitigation for the information-disclosure risk row; it cannot discharge that. COR-007 additionally reports at this line that public From throws on DestinationRefusal.None, so an accidental call on the success path turns a 201 into a 500.
findings.suggestion: Serialize the whole record including Errors and drive the test from an address-bearing input capable of failing it. Make From private so FromOrNull is the only public entry.
findings.reason: Deferred with the highs. Noted specifically because the handover cites this test as a mitigation it cannot provide — the risk row should be corrected when this is fixed.

findings.title: The empty-host guard is untested and is what stops an empty host reaching DNS
findings.description: No test input has a permitted scheme and an empty host, so the guard's true branch has never executed. Deleting it keeps the suite green while the service begins resolving empty strings.
findings.suggestion: Add a case with a permitted scheme and no authority, paired with an orchestration case asserting the resolver is not called.

findings.title: The IsIPv6SiteLocal arm has no test row
findings.description: No test address falls in fec0::/10, so that disjunct has never decided a test and can be deleted without failure.
findings.reason: Folded into the COR-002 fix rather than deferred — the IPv6 range work touches exactly this method and adding one theory row costs nothing while the file is open.

findings.title: A Resolved carrying a null address list throws instead of failing closed
findings.description: The extended property pattern does not match a null Addresses, so control falls to the general arm and dereferences null. IHostResolver is an extension point, so an implementation other than DnsHostResolver can construct this.
findings.suggestion: Match Addresses: null or { Count: 0 } in the first arm.
findings.reason: Deferred with the mediums. Only reachable through a third-party IHostResolver implementation, of which there are none.

findings.title: traceId is accepted unvalidated
findings.description: A whitespace-only identifier produces a structurally valid but undiagnosable error body. It matters more than usual here because api.md 4.3 deliberately withholds the address, making traceId the only route from a ticket to the log.

findings.title: The no-I/O assertion checks only public static methods and only Task return types
findings.description: Private helpers are excluded, which is where I/O would most plausibly be added, and a synchronous Dns.GetHostAddresses call would leave the assertion green. The handover cites this test as the mitigation for the layer-boundaries risk row.
findings.suggestion: Rename to match what it checks, or widen to non-public methods and assert the Domain assembly references nothing outside System.*.
findings.reason: Deferred with the mediums. Same class of problem as TST-004 — the handover overstates what a test proves — and both should be fixed together so the risk table can be corrected once.

findings.title: The scheme-relative test asserts a negative that a permitting implementation satisfies
findings.description: Assert.NotEqual(NotAbsoluteUrl, ...) holds if the value were permitted outright. A test whose job is to pin 422-not-400 is satisfied by a 200. The behaviour is saved only by a coincidental overlap with SchemeTests.
findings.reason: Deferred with the mediums. Worth noting this test was itself written as a correction during cycle 1 and the correction was weaker than the thing it replaced.

findings.title: layers.md 2.2 — Api references Infrastructure but has no composition root
findings.description: 2.2 permits an Infrastructure reference only for the composition root, and Program.cs contains only the scaffold. Nothing registers DnsHostResolver against IHostResolver, so the reference is currently unearned by the exception that would permit it, and any type in the Api can construct the adapter directly.
findings.suggestion: Add the registration, or drop the reference until the registration exists.
findings.reason: Deferred to #18, which is the issue that first needs the handler wired. Adding a composition root here with nothing to compose would be scaffolding ahead of a caller.

findings.title: STD-ARCH-03 — the scaffold route has no version prefix
findings.description: app.MapGet("/", ...) left by dotnet new web. api.md 2.1: 'A route with no version prefix must not be added.' It is the first route in the repository and it is non-conforming.
findings.reason: Folded into the remediation pass rather than deferred. It is a one-line deletion of template scaffolding, the same class as the xunit UnitTest1 stubs removed in cycle 1, and leaving a known-non-conforming route as the repository's only route invites it to be copied.

summary.note: Eight addressed: the six criticals plus TST-007 and ARCH-002, both folded in because they touch files the critical fixes already open. Ten deferred, each with a reason. None ignored. SEC-001 is addressed by waiver WVR-001 rather than by code — the deviation is now recorded, scoped, approved and time-bounded rather than being an unrecorded exception. COR-007 is not a separate entry: it was merged into TST-004 at DestinationProblem.cs:29 and is described there. An earlier draft of this summary counted it twice, giving 19.
